topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's themes and outlines the learning outcomes regarding cellular transformation, cancer genetics, and genomic instability.

topics.label: Tumor virology, proto-oncogenes, and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the historical study of tumor viruses led to the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays for cellular transformation.

topics.label: Oncogenes, tumor suppressor genes, and mutation mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional classifications of cancer-associated mutations and examine how allele dosage and pathway disruption drive abnormal cell cycle progression.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genomic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the distinctions between sequence and chromosomal instability, detailing the DNA repair failures, replication errors, and mitotic defects that cause them.

topics.label: Multistep tumor progression and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the stepwise accumulation of somatic and inherited mutations drives tumorigenesis and influences tumor evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the presentation by reviewing the learning outcomes, taking questions, and recommending supplementary reading.
